recent_posts.title: AI Interview Success: An Interviewer's Inside Guide
recent_posts.summary: An interviewer at Canva shares insights on succeeding in AI-assisted programming interviews. The guide emphasizes using AI tools strategically while maintaining technical ownership and engineering judgment. Key success factors include thoughtful problem-solving, understanding generated code, and demonstrating production-quality standards. Common pitfalls include over-focusing on AI capabilities, rushing through features, or delegating too much to AI. The evaluation focuses on engineering problem-solving, technical depth, and effective AI collaboration rather than AI proficiency alone.

recent_posts.title: From Intern Project to Production: How I Shipped the Draw Tool for Canva's Present Mode
recent_posts.summary: A frontend engineer shares their journey of evolving an internship project into a production feature at Canva. The draw tool for present mode faced three main technical challenges: tightly coupled code requiring architectural refactoring with a new shared package, scaling issues across dual windows solved through coordinate normalization, and performance regression addressed via lazy loading. The feature achieved strong adoption with 10 million uses over two weeks and 470K monthly active users.

recent_posts.title: Measuring Commercial Impact at Scale at Canva
recent_posts.summary: Canva built the IMPACT app using Streamlit in Snowflake to standardize commercial impact measurement across thousands of experiments. The tool reduced analysis time from 6+ hours to under 10 minutes by automating calculations for key metrics like Monthly Active Users and Annual Recurring Revenue. The solution includes a modular architecture with Snowpark for performance optimization, Cortex for natural language summaries, and a custom PR-based development environment enabling safe collaboration across multiple developers.

recent_posts.title: Canva redesigns technical interviews to require AI tool usage
recent_posts.summary: Canva has redesigned their technical interviews to require candidates to use AI tools like Copilot, Cursor, and Claude. The company moved away from traditional algorithm-focused interviews after recognizing that nearly half their engineers use AI daily. Instead of trying to detect AI usage, they embrace transparency and evaluate how well candidates collaborate with AI to solve complex, ambiguous problems. The new format assesses skills like breaking down requirements, making technical decisions with AI assistance, and critically reviewing AI-generated code. Early results show the approach provides better predictive signals about candidate performance while reflecting the reality of modern software development.

recent_posts.title: Behind the scenes of Canva's DesignDNA campaign
recent_posts.summary: Canva launched its DesignDNA year-in-review campaign in December 2024 using generative AI to create personalized, shareable content showcasing users' achievements. The campaign matched users to emerging 2025 design trends and generated unique content like personalized poems and design personalities, all while adhering to strict user data privacy policies. The effort involved analyzing user behavior and employing AI to ensure each user's experience was distinctive and engaging.

recent_posts.title: Image replacement in Canva designs using reverse image search
recent_posts.summary: Canva implemented a scalable similar-image replacement system using reverse image search to maintain their high-quality image library. This involved selecting a model for image embeddings, experimenting with five high-performing models, and ultimately choosing DINOv2 for its superior results in preserving image subjects and background. The new system significantly speeds up image replacement in templates and is now integrated into Canva's Template Assistant, allowing for human review and quality control. Future improvements may include better handling of symbolic and text-heavy images.

recent_posts.title: The foundations of Canva’s continuous data platform with Snowpipe Streaming
recent_posts.summary: Canva leveraged Snowpipe Streaming to build a continuous data platform, significantly reducing their data processing costs by 45%. They transitioned from AWS Data Firehose to Snowpipe Streaming for better cost efficiency and to handle high data volumes. Integration with Kinesis Data Streams was key, allowing real-time data streaming directly into Snowflake tables. This approach has enabled them to process over 20.35 PiB of data in a cost-effective manner with minimal latency, optimizing their platform for scalability and performance.

recent_posts.title: Canva incident report: API Gateway outage
recent_posts.summary: On November 12, 2024, Canva experienced a critical outage due to API Gateway failures caused by a combination of deployment issues with Canva's editor, network issues with Cloudflare, and a performance bug in their telemetry library. The outage affected canva.com, causing it to be unavailable for nearly an hour. Canva implemented several mitigation strategies during the incident, including scaling API Gateway tasks and blocking traffic at the CDN level. In response, Canva has outlined improvements to their incident response process, API Gateway resilience, telemetry bug fixes, and collaboration with Cloudflare to prevent future occurrences.

recent_posts.title: The science of routing print orders
recent_posts.summary: Canva's Print team built a configurable rules system for graph traversal to optimize the routing of print orders. This system ensures efficient delivery times and reduced environmental impact by determining the best production and shipping routes. The architecture comprises three main subsystems for building and retrieving graph structures, decision-making, and traversal. With a focus on customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and engineering flexibility, the system uses relational databases and asynchronous processes to maintain data consistency and optimize routing decisions.

recent_posts.title: How to improve search without looking at queries or results
recent_posts.summary: In October 2024, Canva reached 200 million monthly active users, highlighting the need for an effective search function for user designs. Traditional search evaluations use sampled user queries and expert labeling, but Canva prioritizes privacy, avoiding the use of real user data. Instead, they leverage generative AI to create synthetic content, enabling them to test search improvements without compromising privacy. The post discusses building a labeled evaluation dataset using GPT-4, issues encountered, and the development of an evaluation tool for rapid, reproducible offline testing. This allows engineers to confidently assess changes locally before online experimentation, enhancing iteration speed and result reliability.
